H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper describes a three-level control architecture and modes within gait states, but the supervisory FSM itself is a flat 2/3/4/5-state gait partition, not an explicit composite-state FSM.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Multiple threshold guards are specified: FSR threshold for stance/swing, negative velocity threshold for early-to-middle stance and early-to-late swing, and positive velocity threshold for mid-to-late stance.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: State/mode outputs include phase-specific constant extension torque, Zero-mode friction compensation, impedance torque, and Adaptive torque proportional to estimated biological knee moment.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The system includes an emergency switch that can immediately cut off power, but the paper does not define a full recovery state hierarchy.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: State names and modes are introduced in Control, phase-specific torque assignments appear in Experimental Evaluation/Results, and guard details are reported in the validation text around Figure 4.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as stance, swing, Zero mode, and Adaptive mode are operationally explained by thresholds or torque behavior rather than requiring unstated domain decoding.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions such as assistance during stance/late swing or mid-stance/late swing are described narratively in validation sections, not in a co-located state-action table.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The transition guards are single-sensor threshold comparisons on FSR or knee angular velocity; no multi-variable boolean or arithmetic transition guard is given.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No parent/composite state has its own entry, during, or exit behavior beyond child states; the hierarchy is a control-layer architecture, not a composite FSM.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: The emergency switch is a system-level escape that immediately cuts power regardless of the current gait phase.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: There is no explicit composite-state initialization or pseudo-state routing problem.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: The guards are simple threshold comparisons, so SMT-style multi-variable guard consistency checking offers little unique advantage.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: The emergency cut-off applies across all gait phases, so a forced transition could encode one global escape instead of duplicating it per state.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: The outputs are concrete knee torque/current/control commands, not abstract log, publish, notify, or operator-message actions.

key_nl_quotes: The FSM is flexible... split the gait cycle in four different ways
An emergency switch... immediately cut off power from the system
one_line_pitch: A sensor-guarded gait FSM with phase-specific torque actions and a global emergency cut-off stresses action attribution and cross-section synthesis more than hierarchy.
rationale: This is a meaningful stress-test sample because it has multiple real sensor-threshold transitions and rich state/mode-dependent torque actions. Its main difficulty is action attribution across paper sections, plus the global emergency cut-off, both of which are known weaknesses for baseline state-machine extraction. It is better as a backup than a top candidate because the FSM is mostly flat and lacks multi-variable arithmetic guards or true composite-state behavior.
